briefing.opening: Hello everyone. We will now begin the climate briefing for October 3, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis and Economic Warnings
sections.content: Today's main news concerns warnings about the severe impact of the climate crisis across our society and its economic ramifications. Domestically, the climate crisis is shattering the 'resilience illusion' within South Korea's supply chains and corporate strategies [2]. An energy debate is also emerging, where the goal of becoming an 'AI powerhouse' clashes with 'carbon neutrality' targets due to the energy consumption of AI data centers [8]. Internationally, the President of the Dutch Central Bank stated that the economic impact of climate change is no longer deniable [45], alongside observations that climate change is already incurring immense costs [34], and the significance of ongoing climate change-related lawsuits in the U.S. Supreme Court was emphasized [35]. Furthermore, research indicates that historical fossil fuel emissions could influence global warming until 2500 [44]. The severity of the climate crisis is being reported in various fields, including trends in mosquito-borne diseases due to deepening climate change [32] and its effects on mental health [37]. Voices are also calling for a societal shift towards a 'life-centered' approach [3, 40, 47].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation Efforts
sections.content: Amidst this crisis, concrete efforts for climate change adaptation and mitigation continue domestically. The Korea Energy Agency is exploring methods to verify the greenhouse gas reduction performance of climate policies [1], explaining that climate change adaptation reduces damages while mitigation lowers the root causes [4]. Local communities are demonstrating notable adaptation efforts, such as Yeonggwang-gun establishing shelters for outdoor workers in response to the climate crisis [5], and Cheongyang-gun activating an agricultural product price safety net to protect farm household incomes even amidst extreme weather events like heatwaves, droughts, and heavy rainfall [6]. Several local governments are pursuing specific plans for achieving carbon neutrality. The Busan-Jinhae Free Economic Zone Authority is collaborating with seven organizations to foster carbon-neutral industries and create an ecosystem for new ports [9, 12, 15]. Nowon-gu shared its achievements as a leading carbon-neutral city at the '2nd EU Green Day' event [10]. Anyang City and Gwacheon City are also accelerating carbon neutrality efforts by exploring directions for carbon-neutral garden cities and holding final reports on regional energy plans [11, 17]. Incheon citizens are actively participating in shaping the future, presenting a blueprint for Incheon's future as a 'Carbon-Neutral Smart Ocean City' by 2045 [7, 14]. Korea Southern Power Co., Ltd. (KOSPO) is simultaneously addressing carbon neutrality and improving dam water quality by utilizing livestock manure as power generation fuel [16].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Facing Challenges
sections.content: Domestically and internationally, the transition to renewable energy is continuously accelerating, yet it simultaneously faces several challenges. Uljin-gun is discussing the growth of nuclear, hydrogen, and renewable energy and exploring development strategies through the 2026 Future Energy Forum [18, 20]. Goheung-gun has initiated efforts to usher in a 10GW renewable energy era through a 'grand civic compromise' [19, 28]. Jeonnam Development Corporation and Korea Western Power Co., Ltd. are jointly developing onshore and offshore wind power in Gwangju and Jeonnam to expand the renewable energy supply base [27, 29]. Jeju Energy Corporation has commenced development of clean hydrogen production technology to respond to renewable energy fluctuations [22]. While market revitalization is anticipated, with the advent of a contract market system for renewable energy facilities and the projected growth of the metering module market [21, 26], social consensus and coordination during policy implementation remain crucial challenges, as evidenced by the spreading opposition from the agricultural sector due to the push for mandatory renewable energy facility deployment by the Korea Rural Community Corporation [24]. Meanwhile, international energy market changes are also being observed, such as Portugal's Galp Energia considering options for selling renewable energy assets [23].

sections.title: 🌍 International Climate Action and Policy Discussions
sections.content: The international community is actively pursuing various levels of action and policy discussions to address climate change. The City of Cincinnati is supporting residents combating climate change with approximately $1 million, encouraging community adaptation efforts [31]. UNESCO is emphasizing the importance of education, aiming to place it at the core of climate action at COP31 [43]. In technological innovation, a blue pigment catalyst has shown new potential for directly converting carbon dioxide into methane [36]. Meanwhile, there have been instances of papers questioning carbon dioxide and climate change being retracted [30], and policy and scientific debates surrounding climate change continue, with active discussions among politicians worldwide regarding their climate and energy policy stances [38, 41, 42]. Fishing communities are proposing priorities for climate change adaptation and exploring field-oriented response measures [46]. News of students winning a climate change storytelling competition [48] and a Fijian climate activist's message at a UN conference [49] reflect the diverse voices within the international community regarding climate action.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the severity of the climate crisis and the various domestic and international efforts to address it. We must strengthen climate resilience through continuous scientific research and policy efforts. This concludes today's climate briefing.
